content.value_statement: HyperFrames projects can become difficult to edit when scenes and media create unlabeled timeline rows. This skill defines track grouping, scene composition, caption placement, and safe-zone rules for Studio.
actual_capabilities: Organizes top-level elements into readable Studio timeline rows.
Defines one sub-composition for each scene with nested structure.
Consolidates captions into one dedicated caption track.
Groups video, graphics, captions, and audio by element kind.
Applies action-safe and title-safe placement rules for wide and vertical framing.
Provides a lint and Studio review checklist for validating timeline structure.
limitations: It does not describe individual edits such as trimming, splitting, or retiming.
It does not generate media, captions, or project files by itself.
It does not replace Studio preview inspection or project-specific lint rules.
It does not define custom safe margins beyond the documented defaults.

use_cases.title: Plan a Studio-ready composition
use_cases.description: Use the track and scene rules before building a HyperFrames project so editors can navigate the resulting timeline.

use_cases.title: Review timeline structure
use_cases.description: Check an existing project for misplaced nested markup, mixed track kinds, or duplicated caption rows before opening it in Studio.

use_cases.title: Protect captions and key content
use_cases.description: Apply action-safe and title-safe boundaries when designing wide, vertical, two-up, or split layouts.

prompt_templates.title: Set up a basic timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me structure this HyperFrames project for Studio. Identify the base video, scenes, captions, and audio, then recommend one track for each kind.

prompt_templates.title: Separate scenes correctly
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my composition outline and list which scenes require separate sub-compositions. Explain why each nested structure should be isolated.

prompt_templates.title: Audit caption placement
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this project description against the one-caption-track rule and the title-safe boundary. List each issue and the structural correction.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a final Studio check
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise validation checklist for this HyperFrames project. Cover track kinds, track indexes, scene hosts, safe zones, lint results, and Studio preview review.

output_examples.input: A project has separate rows for each caption group and mixes music with graphics.
output_examples.output: Move every caption group into one captions sub-composition. Keep music on an audio row and graphics on a graphics row.

output_examples.input: A title and subtitle remain nested inside the root composition.
output_examples.output: Create a scene sub-composition for the title and subtitle. Keep only its timed host in the root composition.

output_examples.input: A vertical layout places captions near the frame edge.
output_examples.output: Move captions and key content inside the 80 percent title-safe box. Keep all visible content inside the 90 percent action-safe box.

best_practices: Design the root composition around timed hosts, media, and audio.
Validate track grouping with lint before reviewing the project in Studio.
Keep captions and important content inside the documented safe boxes.
anti_patterns: Do not create one top-level row for every caption group.
Do not mix captions, graphics, video, or audio on the same track.
Do not place nested scene markup or guide overlays directly in the root composition.

faq.question: What does this skill organize?
faq.answer: It organizes HyperFrames composition structure for readable timelines in Studio.

faq.question: Should every scene become a sub-composition?
faq.answer: Every scene with nested structure should become its own sub-composition.

faq.question: How many caption tracks should a project use?
faq.answer: Use one caption track containing every caption group in sequence.

faq.question: Which elements share a track kind?
faq.answer: Group base video, graphics, captions, and audio by their documented element kind.

faq.question: What are the safe-zone defaults?
faq.answer: Keep visible content within the 90 percent action-safe box and key content within the 80 percent title-safe box.

faq.question: Does this skill teach clip editing?
faq.answer: No. Use the dedicated HyperFrames editing guidance for splitting, trimming, retiming, volume, copying, or swapping.
